# Sirach Chapter 41 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 41 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**41:1** O death, how bitter is the thought of you to one who is at peace in his possessions, to the man who has no worries and is prosperous in all things, and who still has the strength to appreciate food!

**41:2** O death, how welcome is your sentence to one who is in need and whose strength fails, who is extremely old and burdened with anxieties about everything, to one who is cantankerous and has lost all patience!

**41:3** Do not fear the sentence of death; remember those who came before you and those who will come after. This is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.

**41:4** And why do you resist the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it is ten years or a hundred or a thousand — there is no recrimination in Hades about the length of one's life.

**41:5** The children of sinners are detestable children, and they congregate in the haunts of the ungodly.

**41:6** The inheritance of sinners' children shall be destroyed, and perpetual disgrace shall cling to their offspring.

**41:7** Children denounce an ungodly father, because they bear reproach on his account.

**41:8** Woe to you, O ungodly men, who have abandoned the law of the Most High God!

**41:9** When you are born, you are born into cursing; and when you die, cursing is your lot.

**41:10** All that is from the earth returns to the earth; so the ungodly go from curse to ruin.

**41:11** The mourning of men is over their bodies, but the evil name of sinners shall be blotted out.

**41:12** Have regard for your name, for it will outlast you longer than thousands of great hoards of gold.

**41:13** The days of a good life are numbered, but a good name endures forever.

**41:14** My children, keep instruction in peace; hidden wisdom and concealed treasure — what is the use of either?

**41:15** Better is the person who hides his folly than the one who hides his wisdom.

**41:16** Therefore show proper shame regarding the things I am about to speak of, for it is not good to show partiality in every matter:

**41:17** Be ashamed before father and mother of sexual immorality, and before a ruler and a person of power of a falsehood;

**41:18** before a master and a mistress of a trespass; before an assembly and a people of a lawless deed;

**41:19** before a companion and friend of injustice; and in the place where you live, of theft.

**41:20** Be ashamed of the truth of God and his covenant, and of resting on your elbow at table;

**41:21** of selfishness in receiving and giving, and of silence before those who greet you;

**41:22** of looking at a prostitute, and of turning your face away from a kinsman;

**41:23** of taking away someone's share and not returning it, and of setting your eye on another man's wife;

**41:24** of meddling with his servant girl — and do not approach her bed;

**41:25** of reproachful words before friends, and after giving something, of taunting;

**41:26** of repeating what you have heard and disclosing secrets.

**41:27** Then you will be truly modest, and you will find favor with every person.
